item.text: {"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"For the 2023 period, movement toward Sisi’s stated or reliably revealed goals was mixed, with outcome attribution and distributional progress uncertain. Security outcomes moved favorably in North Sinai: ISIL-Sinai conducted fewer than ten attacks and the peninsula was reported less violent than in the preceding decade, but casualty reporting was restricted, residents remained displaced, and the United States supplied significant counterterrorism assistance; durability and Sisi-specific contribution therefore remain qualified (BATCH-0006-E009; BATCH-0006-E010; BATCH-0022-E011). Social-protection coverage was reported at 4.67 million households by December 2023, while a separate September government figure reported more than five million families; these figures use different dates and are not directly comparable. In either case, the coverage represented only about one-third of families living in or near poverty, and currency devaluation made transfers inadequate against inflation and low baseline social spending (BATCH-0020-E012; BATCH-0009-R07-E009; BATCH-0009-R07-E010; BATCH-0009-R11-E004). Universal health-insurance enrollment exceeded five million people in six Phase 1 governorates, but the reported cumulative result is not dated specifically to year-end 2023 and implementation was supported by the World Bank, so it establishes program reach rather than a Sisi-attributable outcome improvement (BATCH-0023-E003). A World Bank study credited improved public transport with a 4 percent Greater Cairo air-pollution reduction, but the evidence does not identify the responsible projects or isolate presidential causation (BATCH-0009-R10-E005). Against these limited or qualified gains, 2023 brought inflation of 39.7 percent, a roughly 50 percent currency depreciation over 22 months, severe poverty, nationwide electricity cutbacks that appeared longer in rural and impoverished areas, and continuing water and agricultural stress. Wheat and corn yields declined by 30–40 percent, the orange harvest was nearly ruined, and military-managed reclamation showed lower wheat yields than comparison areas while raising aquifer-depletion, salinity, contamination, and land-degradation concerns (BATCH-0006-E016; BATCH-0007-E020; BATCH-0009-R07-E011; BATCH-0009-R10-E007; BATCH-0009-R10-E015). The government and Sisi attributed deterioration partly to COVID-19, the Ukraine war, global prices, higher interest rates, and capital outflows, while other analyses identify domestic policy choices, military-led megaprojects, debt financing, weak productive investment, mismanagement, and inadequate social protection as additional plausible causes (BATCH-0003-E013; BATCH-0020-E010; BATCH-0009-R11-E006; BATCH-0015-E008).
